# qr-multi-imgs

> A QR code scanner that reads a whole folder of images at once, in the
> browser, without uploading anything. Also a command line tool.

Site: https://thousandflowers.github.io/qr-multi-imgs/
Source: https://github.com/thousandflowers/qr-multi-imgs
Licence: MIT

## What it does

- Reads every QR code in every image of a folder, a zip, or a single photo.
- Reads every code in one image, not only the first.
- Scans live from a camera, several codes in the same frame at once.
- Lets a person draw a box around a code the automatic pass could not read,
  and reads that area on its own.
- Exports the results as CSV, JSON or plain text.
- Recreates any code it read as PNG, JPEG, SVG or PDF.
- Turns a column of a CSV file into a batch of QR codes.
- Names the site a link leads to before opening it, and warns about addresses
  built to imitate another one.
- Renames image files after the code they contain.

## What is true about privacy

Nothing is uploaded. The decoder is WebAssembly compiled from Go and runs
inside the tab. The page ships a Content Security Policy whose connect-src
allows only its own origin and the loopback address, so the page cannot send a
filename or a payload to any third party. There is no account, no analytics
and no third-party script, font or image.

## How it differs from other QR readers

Most read one picture at a time and stop at the first code in it. This one
takes a folder and returns every code in every image with the file it came
from, which is the shape of the job when someone has photographed a wall of
posters, a stack of invoices, or a box of parts.

## Languages

English, Italian, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, and Chinese in both
Simplified and Traditional. The two Chinese blocks are written separately
rather than converted, because the vocabulary differs and not only the
characters.

## The command line version

  brew install thousandflowers/tap/qr-multi-imgs
  qr-multi-imgs ~/Pictures/scans --json

Runs on macOS, Linux and Windows. On macOS it also uses Apple Vision, which
reads codes the pure-Go decoder misses.
